newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end dull trade mostly weaker.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end dull trade mostly weaker.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended low-volume trading weaker, with market holidays in some centers cutting deeply into volume.
"It was a pretty inactive day," said one floor broker after the close.
They said the market was waiting to see which direction traders in Japan and the United Kingdom take the market when they return Tuesday.
Several players looked for more currency downside soon, given sentiment that U.S. rates are headed higher and that a U.S. budget pact could add to the dollar's attractiveness.
The proposed budget, which needs Congressional passage, includes a capital gains tax cut and other relief measures.
Nearby yen and sterling cut losses late after failing to extend on the downside early, but turnover there stayed subdued, brokers said.
Instead, a broker said a Japanese-owned firm bought about 500 June Canadian dollar futures in the closing range, helping buoy a contract that he said has a strong technical outlook.
Futures earlier had tested the downside and stalled, with June marks slipping below support near $0.5797 or 1.73 spot, while one fund manager sold some 600 June yen.
Televised comments Sunday by U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin, in which he reiterated that he "did agree" with Japan's recently expressed concern about the yen's weakness, had little effect.
Traders waited for Wednesday's monetary meeting between Bank of England governor Eddie George and new chancellow Gordon Brown. They are expected to agree to hike U.K. rates.

June yen rose $0.000002 to $0.007951, marks lost $0.0011 to $0.5790, Swiss franc lost $0.0018 to $0.6809, sterling rose $0.0024 to 1.6226, Can dollar added $0.0004 to $0.7262, Aussie dollar lost $0.0033 to $0.7798, M peso up $0.000100 to $0.124475.
